transportOverlay.note: Transport-only overlay. The bytes moved in the historical 2026-11-18 re-pin: `d1619cce...`/2,613 B is superseded by `533b3120...`/3,191 B. It no longer pins one FHGFF3 file identity: FHGM-Specification#17 (maintainer dual-base decision of 2026-11-15) rewrote it as a closed `anyOf` of two branch pairings, and FHGM-Specification#26 (019bc29e, the overlay's own last-touched commit; byte-identical at the pinned 06176262) widened the v0.6.0 branch: the pairing is now the v0.5.0 citation set with `schemaVersion` '1.1', or the v0.6.0 citation set with '1.2' **or '1.1'** - the v0.6.0 release accepts 1.1 records per the shared docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md - and the v0.6.0 URI set gained the raw tag URL under the FHR-Specification historical repository name, which the shared release recognises. A citation and a stated version that contradict each other (a v0.5.0 citation stating 1.2) stay rejected, and neither branch falls back to the other; `test/fhgm.test.mjs` covers the three admitted pairings, the contradiction and the inadmissible 1.0. FHGM carriers may now cite a release-tag URL of the *released* FHGFF3 contract - that is the carrier's own file identity under V2/V3, a released contract, and not a release form of the unreleased FHGM draft; the `fhr-specification-alias-v0.6.0` and `v0.6.0-citation-stating-1.1` vectors pin exactly that reading (rule V7 is about the draft's own citation, which stays raw-main-only). The overlay says nothing about record contents: those are the model contract above. It still requires a non-empty `x-fhgm-models` array of objects. This changes a documented divergence rather than recording a new number: `docs/CAPABILITY.md` and `src/fhgm.js` answered the pairing question for the two-branch overlay, and the pinned bytes now answer it for three pairings, which is why those rows and `test/fhgm.test.mjs` moved with this re-pin instead of being left to rot.

FHGM.laneStanding: Measured 2026-11-19 (Round 14 #23) against the same pinned bytes (suite 06176262, manifest e41f05fd…): 62 pass / 0 fail / 0 not-run. The four expectations FHGM-Specification#29 added, named as failures in the verification above, are implemented in this build: K1 refuses a carrier whose cited schema URL is not a registered base release of the pinned overlay (raw main, v0.4.0, or missing); K4 targets only a root gene row — a Parent= with no value or a bare Parent token is indeterminate and rejects — and decodes row ID= over raw bytes with strict UTF-8, so an un-decodable escape such as %FF is unaddressable, while the record's featureId is compared as written; K3 compares modelIds after Unicode NFC normalisation, after the whole-record K2 pass and before per-record K4/K5. These implement the FHGM#29 reading of a DRAFT: FHGM-Specification#22/#27/#28/#32 remain open upstream and an accepted decision can move the expectations; this field names the bytes this build answers to, not a settled rule text. The 2026-11-18 verification above is retained as the dated measurement it was.
